# The Cold That Makes the Stars Speak

## Scripture

*"The heavens declare the glory of God; the skies proclaim the work of his hands. Day after day they pour forth speech; night after night they reveal knowledge. They have no speech, they use no words; no sound is heard from them. Yet their voice goes out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world."* — Psalm 19:1–4

## Reflection

On a clear November night, if you step outside and let your eyes adjust, you may notice that the stars seem sharper than they did in summer. This isn't your imagination. Cold air holds less moisture, and the haze that softens summer skies has settled out of the atmosphere. The same stars, seen through clearer air, appear brighter and more numerous. Winter's chill, which we so often resent, is what makes the heavens most articulate.

The psalmist knew something of this. He looked up and heard the skies *speaking*—not with words, but with a voice that carries to the ends of the earth. And notice: they speak most clearly not in spite of the cold, but often because of it. The crisp, uncomfortable nights are the ones that reveal the most.

Perhaps God works the same way in us. Seasons that feel barren or biting can actually clear away the haze—the distractions, the comfortable fog—and let His glory come through sharper than before. The psalm doesn't say the heavens shout only on pleasant evenings. Day after day, night after night, they pour forth speech. Even the cold ones. Even yours.

## Prayer

Lord of the heavens, thank You that even in the cold and clarity of difficult seasons, Your glory speaks. Clear away the haze in my heart, and give me eyes to see Your handiwork—especially when the nights feel long and sharp. Let my life, like the skies, declare Your praise. Amen.
